lesson_title: The Notebook or the Count: Inventory Systems
hook_text: A case of energy drinks walks out the back door. One shop notices. The other calls it a sale.
clip_script: Two tuck-shop owners, one taxi rank between them, two ways of running stock. The first keeps a notebook: every time a two-litre cooldrink goes over the counter, she writes down not only the R25 she took, but that a bottle costing R18 left the shelf. Any hour of any day, she knows what should be standing on her shelves. The second keeps no notebook — he records what he buys, takes the money at the till, and at year end he locks the door, counts everything still standing, and does one sum: what I started with, plus what I bought, minus what is still here — that must be what I sold. Both reach a number. But watch what the second owner surrendered. If a case of energy drinks slipped out the back door in August, his sum calmly calls it SOLD — because there is nothing left to count and nothing to compare against. Her notebook would have said: R2 100 of drinks should be here. His system says: business was just a little disappointing this year.
visual_style: Two tuck-shop counters side by side; one with a glowing running tally floating above the shelves, the other dark until a year-end torch sweep counts the shelves; a case of energy drinks sliding out a back door and dissolving silently into one owner's cost-of-sales bar.
mood: Quietly revealing — a small story with a sharp control lesson.
pacing: Parallel-story rhythm, one beat per system, hard landing on the stolen case.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the year-end sum yourself.
